Condition : 1 - The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.
Reason: To accord with the provisions of Section 92(1) of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

Condition : 2 - The development hereby permitted, comprising 85 care home bed-spaces and associated accommodation and works, in addition to 172 square metres of Class E retail floorspace, shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans and specifications:

Condition : 4 - Notwithstanding any details provided in the documents hereby approved and prior to first occupation of the development, finalised details of the proposed shopfront and Acton Lane care home frontages (including 1:20 bay studies, finalised elevations, a materials schedule and details of any pilasters, cornicing, stall risers/plinths, canopies and glazing etc.) shall have been submitted to the local planning authority for approval in writing, in consultation with Part A2 ('Shopfronts and Public Buildings' section) of the Council's Character, Sustainability and Design Codes Supplementary Planning Document.
Reason: In order to protect the appearance of the conservation area.

Condition : 5 - No external utility boxes (for gas and electricity) shall be affixed to the building and any cables, wires, aerials, pipework, meter boxes or flues shall be discreetly integrated into the building and shall not be fixed to any elevation or roof slope facing a highway. 
No fans, louvres, ducts, water tanks or other external plant shall be installed on the building hereby permitted without the prior written approval of the local planning authority. 
No advertisements shall be displayed on the development without details of the advertisements having first been submitted to and approved in writing by the Council through securing of Advertisement Consent and/or Planning Permission. 
Reason: In order to safeguard the visual amenity of the area and neighbours living conditions.

Condition : 6 - Supporting Notes (Lighting Strategy): Where possible, use of low UV warm-white LED bulbs with directional, downward facing and shielded lights for sections is encouraged, especially adjacent to sensitive receptors (e.g. residential dwellings). Internal luminaires can be recessed where installed in proximity to windows to reduce glare and light spill or treated with low transmission glazing. Lights in the public realm should be subject to curfew controls where possible with lights on movement sensors to reduce light pollution when not needed.

Condition : 8 - Prior to first occupation of the development, details (e.g. photographs and copies of installation contracts) shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing, to demonstrate that the development has been carried out in accordance with the following sustainable sourcing of materials requirements:
-	At least three of the key elements of the building envelope (external walls, windows roof, upper floor slabs, internal walls, floor finishes/coverings) are to achieve a rating of A+ to D in the Building Research Establishment (BRE) The Green Guide of specification. 
- 	At least 50% of timber and timber products are to be sourced from accredited Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) or Programme for the Endorsement of Forestry Certification (PEFC) scheme. 
- 	No construction or insulation materials are to be used which would release toxins into the internal and external environment, including those that deplete stratospheric ozone. 
Reason: In order to ensure the sustainable sourcing of materials.

Condition : 9 - a)	The development hereby permitted shall be implemented in accordance with the hereby approved Sustainability and Energy Strategy Report (Rev P02) dated 2 December 2024 and associated documentation including the submitted 'Planning Supplementary Information Sustainability Response' dated 28 February 2025. 
b)	Prior to first occupation of the development, evidence (e.g. photographs, installation contracts and As-Built certificates under the Standard Assessment Procedure/National Calculation Method) shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority to show that these areas of development have been constructed in accordance with the approved Energy Statement to achieve a site-wide carbon reduction in emissions of at least 37% on Part L Building Regulations. 
c)	Upon final commencement of operation of any low and zero carbon technologies, suitable devices for the monitoring of the low and zero carbon technologies shall have been installed, and the monitored data shall be submitted automatically to a monitoring web-platform at daily intervals for a period of three years from the point of full operation.
Reason: To ensure that the development makes the fullest contribution to minimising carbon dioxide emissions.

Condition : 10 - Prior to first occupation of the development, full details of the proposed heat pumps shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. These shall include:
-	An estimate of the heating and/or cooling energy (MWh/annum) the heat pumps would provide to the development and the percentage of contribution to the site's heat loads to demonstrate how the heat fraction from heat pump technologies has been maximised.
-	Details of the Seasonal Coefficient of Performance (SCOP) and/or Seasonal Energy Efficiency ratio (SEER) and how these have been calculated including the expected heat source and heat distribution temperatures (for space heat and hot water) and the distribution loss factor, which shall be calculated based on the above information.
-	Details of all screening and acoustic insulation to protect against visual harm and undue noise and disturbance to surrounding sensitive receptors. 
The cumulative measured or calculated rating level of noise emitted from the air source heat pumps hereby approved shall generate no more than 10dB(A) below the existing background noise level, during all times that the mechanical system is in operation. The measured or calculated noise levels shall be determined at the boundary of the nearest ground floor noise sensitive uses or one metre from the facade of the nearest first floor (or higher) noise sensitive uses, and in accordance with the latest British Standard 4142 (or any successor to this). An alternative position for assessment / measurement may be used to allow ease of access; however, this must first be agreed in writing by the local planning authority and illustrated on a map with noise propagation calculations detailed to show how the design criteria is achieved.
The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.
Reason: To achieve appropriate sustainability standards, to protect residents living conditions and to preserve the amenities of the area.

Condition : 11 - A. Prior to commencement of any above-ground works on the development hereby permitted (except any demolition, site clearance, ground investigation and remediation work), details of the specifications regarding power, number, appearance, location, orientation, total area and predicted carbon savings from the photovoltaic panels shall have been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority to show how the renewable energy carbon savings are to be achieved and maximised. The photovoltaic panels shall be installed in accordance with the approved details prior to the occupation of the relevant part of the development and retained and maintained as such unless otherwise agreed by the Local Planning Authority.
B. No solar panels shall be installed until a glint and glare assessment has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. No subsequent alterations to the approved scheme are to take place unless submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: To achieve appropriate sustainability standards and to ensure the development does not endanger the safe movement of aircraft or the operation of Heathrow Airport. The airport requires a glint and glare assessment to be completed to determine the full impact on pilots approaching the airport.

Condition : 12 - (a) Within three months of commencement of the development (except any demolition, site clearance, ground investigation and remediation work), a BREEAM Design Stage certificate and summary score sheet (or such equivalent standard that replaces this) shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority to show that an 'Excellent' (minimum score 70%) rating will be achieved in accordance with approved documents.
(b) Within six months of the date of first occupation of the development, a BREEAM Post-Construction Review certificate and summary score sheet (or such equivalent standard that replaces this) shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority to show that an 'Excellent' (minimum score 70%) rating has been achieved.
Reason: In order to ensure the highest standard of sustainable design and construction.
Supporting notes: 
Details submitted should state if BREEAM will be fully fitted, shell and core or shell only. Additional BREEAM Refurbishment and Fit-Out details will likely be required where not specified as fully fitted.

Condition : 13 - Prior to commencement of groundworks (excluding site investigation, demolition and remediation work), the applicant shall have submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing, in consultation with the Lead Local Flood Authority, a final detailed drainage design including drawings, supporting calculations and an updated Drainage Assessment Form or SuDS Proforma, all aligned with the Surface & Foul Water Drainage Strategy (dated 25 February 2025) and associated submissions hereby approved. This shall include a CCTV survey to verify the exact route, diameter, levels, material, condition and location of the sewer at the site, as specified in the Drainage Strategy. All proposed SuDS features and the total site area should be incorporated into the calculations. It should be demonstrated that on-site flow as a result of the 1 in 100 year event with a climate change consideration must be suitably managed, with exceedance flows directed away from buildings. A detailed management plan confirming routine maintenance tasks for all drainage components (including details of a maintenance owner) must also be submitted to demonstrate how the drainage system is to be maintained for the lifetime of the development. Consent from Thames Water for the proposed discharge connection must be provided, with details provided about how surface water discharge would take place. 
Reason: To prevent the risk of flooding to and from the site.

Condition : 14 - No part of the development hereby permitted shall be occupied until evidence (photographs and installation contracts) has been submitted to the local planning authority and approved in writing to demonstrate that the sustainable drainage scheme for the site has been completed in accordance with the submitted details. The sustainable drainage scheme shall be managed and maintained thereafter in accordance with the agreed management and maintenance plan for all of the proposed drainage components.
Reason: To prevent the risk of flooding to and from the site.

Condition : 15 - A programme of archaeological work must be completed as described in the approved Written Scheme of Investigation (Border Archaeology: ref. BA2589(21121)ACT/WSI, June 2025), received on 27/06/2025. For land that is included within the WSI, no demolition or development shall take place other than in accordance with the agreed WSI, and the programme and methodology of site evaluation and the nomination of a competent person(s) or organisation to undertake the agreed works.
If heritage assets of archaeological interest are identified by stage 1 then for those parts of the site which have archaeological interest a stage 2 WSI shall be submitted to and approved by the local planning authority in writing. For land that is included within the stage 2 WSI, no demolition/development shall take place other than in accordance with the agreed stage 2 WSI which shall include:
A.       The statement of significance and research objectives, the programme and methodology of site investigation and recording and the nomination of a competent person(s) or organisation to undertake the agreed works;
B.       Where appropriate, details of a programme for delivering related positive public benefits;
C.       The programme for post-investigation assessment and subsequent analysis, publication and dissemination and deposition of resulting material. This part of the condition shall not be discharged until these elements have been fulfilled in accordance with the programme set out in Stage 2 WSI.
Reason: To safeguard potential archaeological remains on the site. 
Supporting Notes: Written schemes of investigation will need to be prepared and implemented by a suitably professionally accredited archaeological practice in accordance with Historic England's Guidelines for Archaeological Projects in Greater London. This condition is exempt from deemed discharge under schedule 6 of The Town and Country Planning (Development Management Procedure) (England) Order 2015.

Condition : 16 - No piling shall take place until a Piling Method Statement (detailing the depth and type of piling to be undertaken and the methodology by which such piling will be carried out, including measures to prevent and minimise the potential for damage to subsurface sewerage infrastructure, and the programme for the works) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority in consultation with Thames Water. Any piling must be undertaken in accordance with the terms of the approved piling method statement.
Reason: The proposed works will be in close proximity to underground sewerage utility infrastructure. Piling has the potential to significantly impact / cause failure of local underground sewerage utility infrastructure. 
Supporting Notes (from Thames Water):
Please read our guide 'working near our assets' to ensure your workings will be in line with the necessary processes you need to follow if you're considering working above or near our pipes or other structures. 
Should you require further information please contact Thames Water. Email: developer.services@thameswater.co.uk Phone: 0800 009 3921 (Monday to Friday, 8am to 5pm) Write to: Thames Water Developer Services, Clearwater Court, Vastern Road, Reading, Berkshire RG1 8DB.

Condition : 17 - Development shall be carried in accordance with the Preliminary Risk Assessment: Desk Study (Arbtech, dated 3 June 2025), received 07/06/2025, which is hereby approved. 
No development (except any demolition, site clearance, ground investigation and remediation work), other than necessary works to enable intrusive investigations shall take place until a Phase II site investigation report, prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. 
This report shall identify the areas and sources of land contamination that exist on the site and identify the scope of site remediation measures necessary before the development commences.
The investigation shall be carried out by a competent person(s), based on the initial Conceptual Site Model (CSM) and on-site observations, to identify the extent and nature of contaminants. The initial CSM shall be updated accordingly following a tiered risk assessment based on the findings of the investigation, and where applicable, the report shall include proposals to deal with the identified contamination on site. 
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting Notes:
(i)	The report shall include details of such sampling of soil, soil vapour, ground gas, leachate, surface water and/or groundwater at such locations and depths as are considered to characterise the site conditions based on the initial Conceptual Site Model (CSM) and on-site observations during investigation work. 
(ii)	The investigation and the report must adhere to current UK guidance and best practice.
(iii)	Further investigation shall be carried out at such locations and at such depths as the Local Planning Authority may stipulate if this report is found to be insufficient or where

Condition : 18 - If a scheme for remediation is recommended in the Phase II site investigation for the site, no development (except refurbishment of existing buildings, demolition, site clearance, ground investigation and remediation work) shall take place until a remediation method statement prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person to specify the works necessary to render the site suitable for its proposed end use, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. 
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting Notes:
(i)	The remediation method statement shall provide suitable details of how the risks of each pollutant linkages, as identified in the updated Conceptual Site Model, will be mitigated.
(ii)	The report shall account for any comments made by the Local Planning Authority. 
(iii)	Remediation work shall be carried out in accordance with the approved remediation method statement for verification and validation before the development is first brought into use.
(iv)	The Council requests that remediation method statement or site plans be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval.

Condition : 19 - The Local Planning Authority shall be notified immediately if any land contamination not previously identified is encountered during development. A competent person shall assess the contamination, where necessary, including soil and groundwater sampling and testing before any further part of the development that may be affected by the additional contamination that has been discovered continues. 
A revised remediation method statement, prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person, shall be submitted in writing to the Local Planning Authority for approval within one month of the discovery of such contamination. 
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting Notes:
(i)	Further remediation work to remove or manage additional contamination shall be carried out in accordance with the approved revised remediation method statement for verification and validation before the development is first brought into use. 
(ii)	In some instances, the Local Planning Authority may require work on site to be ceased whilst the nature of additional contamination is investigated fully.
(iii)	The Council requests that the revised remediation method statement or any site photos be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval.

Condition : 20 - The agreed scheme for remediation, including any amendments, shall be fully implemented as part of the development. A verification report produced upon completion of the remediation for relevant parts of the development by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person shall be submitted in writing to the Local Planning Authority for approval, before that part of the development is first brought into use or in accordance with a programme approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. 
Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.
Supporting Notes:
(i)	The verification (closure) report shall revisit the conceptual site model and provide evidence that each aspect of the remediation plan has been implemented correctly and successfully in accordance with current UK guidance and best practice. Where applicable, the report shall describe how any additional/unexpected contamination encountered during development has been managed in line with the revised remediation method statement. 
(ii)	This report shall demonstrate that the development is suitable for its proposed use in terms of land quality.
(iii)	The Council requests that the verification report or site photos be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval.

Condition : 21 - If long-term monitoring and maintenance is required following successful completion of approved remedial measures, reports which demonstrate the effectiveness of the monitoring and maintenance shall be prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person and submitted to the Local Planning Authority according to an agreed timescale as shall first have been approved under other conditions set out in this planning approval decision notice. 
This shall be conducted in accordance with current UK guidance and best practice. 
Reason: In order to ensure that risks from land contamination to the future users of the land and neighbouring land are minimised, together with those to controlled waters, properties and ecological systems.

Condition : 22 - Demolition works shall be carried out in strict accordance with the Demolition Environmental Management Plan (dated September 2025), received 19/09/2025, which is hereby approved.
Reason. To ensure highway safety is maintained and preserved and in the interests of air quality and mitigating impacts on neighbouring premises.

Condition : 23 - All Non-road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) used during the course of the development that is within the scope of the GLA 'Control of Dust and Emissions during Construction and Demolition' Supplementary Planning Guidance (SPG) dated July 2014, or any successor document, shall comply with the emissions requirements therein. 
The developer shall keep an up-to-date list of all NRMM used during the demolition, site preparation and construction phases of the development on the online register at https://nrmm.london/. 
Reason: In the interests of preventing harmful air quality impacts.

Condition : 24 - No development (except any demolition, site clearance, ground investigation and remediation work) shall take place until a Construction Method Statement (CMS) relating to the basement hereby approved has been submitted to the Local Planning Authority. The CMS shall be certified by a qualified professional and give details of excavation, temporary works and construction techniques, including details of potential impacts on neighbouring land based on assessment of the geology and hydrology of the area. The approved CMS shall be adhered to throughout the construction period for the development.
Reason: In order to protect the living conditions of neighbouring residents, to minimise flood risk and to ensure highway safety is maintained.

Condition : 26 - No demolition or construction work shall take place on the site except between the hours of 8:00am to 6:00pm on Mondays to Friday and 8:00am to 1:00pm on Saturdays and none shall take place on Sundays and Public Holidays without the prior agreement of the Local Planning Authority. Additionally, HGV deliveries to the site during the course of construction will be restricted to between 9:30am and 3:00pm on Mondays to Fridays, and between 9:30am and 1:00pm on Saturdays, and none shall take place on Sundays and Public Holidays without the prior agreement of the Local Planning Authority.
Reason: To ensure that the proposed development does not prejudice the amenities of the locality and to prevent obstruction and inconvenience to users of the public highway.

Condition : 28 - Before the development hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use, a Delivery and Servicing Plan (including details of vehicle access and egress arrangements and times that servicing shall take place) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall accord with current guidance such as that issued by TfL and include measures required to ensure sufficient arrangements (physical as well as managerial) for the servicing, including refuse collection, of all aspects of the development, the timing of hours for deliveries by motor vehicles and a timetable for implementation. The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the approved details and shall be maintained for the lifetime of the development, unless the prior written approval of the local planning authority is obtained to any variation.
Reason: In the interests of the safety of pedestrians and vehicles, to protect neighbours' living conditions and to support sustainable transport objectives.

Condition : 29 - Prior to first occupation of the development, full and finalised details (including manufacturer's specifications, number, location and design) of the cycle and buggy parking provision for employees and visitors to the development shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The submission shall include details of the buggy spaces proposed, the short-stay cycle parking provision (eight spaces) and the long-stay cycle parking provision (ten spaces). The approved cycle parking details shall conform to current guidance such as the TfL London Cycling Design Standards and the West London Cycle Design Guidance in design and layout, and shall be safeguarded from vehicles. The approved cycle parking provisions shall be fully implemented and made available for use before the first occupation of the development and thereafter retained for use at all times without obstruction.
Reason: To support sustainable transport objectives.

Condition : 30 - No development (except any demolition, site clearance, ground investigation and remediation work) shall take place until full and finalised details of the arrangements for the storing of waste and recycled materials (including details of how the placing of waste and recycled materials in a suitable location for collection would be undertaken and managed, and where vehicles would stop for collections) have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the approved details.
Any refuse and recycling bins, delivery cages, trolleys or other items linked to deliveries and collection in association with the approved development are to be stored within the building(s) at all times and only brought out onto the public highway when deliveries are being made or refuse collected.
Reason: In order to ensure adequate provision for waste and recycling, protect the quality of the local environment and prevent obstruction and inconvenience to users of the development.

Condition : 31 - At least three months before completion of the development hereby approved, full and finalised details of the ecological enhancement, urban greening factor and habitat improvement measures to be adopted shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The submitted information shall show how the anticipated urban greening factor and biodiversity net gain scores set out in the approved 'Landscaping and Urban Greening Overview' (December 2024) and 'Biodiversity Net Gain Calculation' (December 2024) documents are to be delivered and achieved on site (and where possible exceeded), with details provided explaining how the enhancement/landscaping measures will be monitored, managed and maintained, including the long- term design objectives, management responsibilities and maintenance schedules. Details of any bird and bat boxes and other viable ecological enhancements (e.g. nest boxes / bricks/ cups; insect blocks; reptile log piles; hedgehog houses etc.) shall be provided, alongside full details of any lighting proposed to show how this would be designed and positioned to minimise impacts on new planting and habitats being created.  
The scheme as approved shall then be implemented prior to first occupation of any part of the development and shall be maintained thereafter in accordance with the approved details. Any subsequent variations shall be agreed in writing by the local planning authority.
Reason: In the interests of nature conservation and biodiversity.

Condition : 32 - The development shall achieve 'Secured by Design' accreditation awarded by the Design-Out Crime Officer from the Metropolitan Police Service on behalf of the Association of Chief Police Officers (ACPO). Prior to first occupation of the development, evidence of the accreditation achieved shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. 
Reason: To minimise opportunities for crime and to increase safety for residents and people in the locality.

Condition : 33 - a) The cumulative measured or calculated rating level of any noise (LAeq) emitted from the mechanical services plant including heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC), along with any heat pumps or mechanical gates or other mechanical infrastructure to which this permission refers, shall remain at least 10dB(A) below the existing representative background noise level (LA90) at all times that the plant operates. 
The measured or calculated noise levels shall be determined at the boundary of the nearest ground floor noise sensitive premises or one metre from the facade of the nearest first floor (or higher) noise sensitive premises, and in accordance with the latest British Standard 4142. An alternative position for assessment/ measurement may be used to allow ease of access, this must be shown on a map and noise propagation calculations detailed to show how the design criteria are achieved.
b) The plant shall be isolated on adequate proprietary anti-vibration mounts to prevent the structural transmission of vibration and regenerated noise within adjacent or adjoining premises, and these shall be so maintained thereafter. 
c) Following installation of any mechanical services plant described in part (a) of this condition, a post completion noise assessment shall be submitted for approval to the Local Planning Authority which demonstrates the actual measured rating level of plant operating under normal conditions. All measurements shall be made in accordance with the methodology of BS4142: 2014 (Methods for rating and assessing industrial and commercial sound) and/or its subsequent amendments. The post completion report shall be both completed and submitted to the local authority within 28 days of completion of the installation for review. If the plant fails to meet the specified standard, remedial measures shall be put in place immediately and the noise assessment shall be carried out again. This shall be repeated until the assessment has reached the requir

Condition : 34 - Noise breakout from the proposed commercial space and noise-generating elements of the care home to primary living spaces (including bedrooms) contained within the same building shall be no more than LAeq,1hour = 25 dB during the daytime and LAeq,15min = 20 dB during the night-time i.e.10 dB below the internal ambient noise level criteria.
Overall noise levels at the development shall not exceed the criteria set out in BS8233:2014 (or equivalent standards if replaced) for internal rooms and external amenity areas (see in particular the limits in Table 4). LAmax noise levels within bedrooms shall not exceed 45 dB LAmax more than 10 to 15 times per night and all occupiers should have access to amenity spaces where noise levels do not exceed 50dB LAeq,16hours.
Noise from uses and activities within the building / development site at neighbouring noise-sensitive / habitable rooms or private external amenity spaces shall also not exceed the criteria of BS8233:2014 (or equivalent standards if replaced).
Prior to the development being occupied, sound insulation tests shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority, including continuous logged data, to demonstrate compliance with the above criteria. 
Reason: In order to secure acceptable living conditions for residential occupiers of the new care home and protect the living conditions of surrounding residents.

Condition : 35 - Prior to first occupation of the development, a finalised Fire Statement shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority which includes: details of a suitable water supply and proof that all relevant fire hydrants are operable; green roof fire safety measures; evidence that solar PV panel cabling would be suitably supported to avoid obstruction of escape routes and firefighting access due to failure of fixings; details of an appropriate signage system and colour coding for the fire-fighting stair design; details of evacuation lifts (with enhanced repair services running 365 days/24-hour cover to ensure no wheelchair occupiers are trapped if a lift breaks down); confirmation that all external doors to the premises would be fitted with self-closing devices and maintained in an operational condition; and proof that power supplies, electrical wiring and control equipment would have appropriate levels of protection against fire.  Development shall be carried out in accordance with this finalised Statement.
Reason: To ensure appropriate measures in place in the interest of fire safety.

Condition : 36 - Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (as amended) (or any order revoking or re-enacting that order) no change of use, enlargement of the premises or provision of additional structures/buildings within the curtilage of the site shall be carried out without the prior written consent of the Local Planning Authority. 
Reason: In the interests of the amenity of the area and order not that the Local Planning Authority is able to exercise control over future development of the site.

Condition : 37 - The use of the specialist care home element of the premises shall be limited exclusively to purposes specified within the permission, and shall be used for no other purpose. This includes any other purpose within Class C2 of the Schedule to the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (as amended), or any provision equivalent to that Class in any statutory instrument revoking and re-enacting that Order with or without modification.
The ground floor and basement level retail/commercial premises shall be limited exclusively to appropriate uses falling under Use Class E of the Schedule to the Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 (as amended) which are compatible with the care home use and surrounding residential uses.
Reason: The Council is satisfied that the use hereby permitted would not result in detriment to adjoining properties but would wish to control future changes of use within the same Use Class to protect nearby land uses and the character of the area.
description: Erection of a six storey building to create an 85 bed residential specialist care facility (Class C2) and one retail unit, along with landscaping, cycle and waste storage and other associated works, following demolition of the existing buildings.
